A2.text:
Tural wanted to cook a special dinner for his friends. He lived in a nice flat near Nizami Street in Baku. He decided to make a Mexican dinner. He watched one video on the internet and thought it was a piece of cake.

“I can do this easily,” Tural told his sister, Nigar, on the phone.

Tural bought chicken, tomatoes, and a lot of red peppers. He loved spicy food. He chopped the vegetables and started to cook. But he made a big mistake. He cooked a huge portion of chicken, and he put too much pepper in the pan.

He tasted the meat and coughed loudly. His face went red. It was much too hot!

Nigar arrived thirty minutes later to help. She looked at the kitchen. It was very messy.

“What happened here?” she asked.

“I cannot serve this,” Tural said sadly. “My mouth is on fire.”

Nigar laughed. “Do not worry. Let's make something simple.”

They quickly cooked a nice homemade pasta. They added some fresh cheese and sweet tomatoes, but no hot peppers.

When Tural’s friends arrived, they sat at the big table. They ate the pasta and loved it.

“This is delicious,” his friend Elvin said.

“Thank you,” Tural smiled. Next time, he decided, he would not cook without a recipe.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: Tural tries to cook a new dish but needs his sister's help
Tural goes to a Mexican restaurant
questions.why: Tural tries to make Mexican food, ruins it, and his sister helps him make pasta instead.

questions.q: What kind of food did Tural want to make first?
questions.why: “He decided to make a Mexican dinner.”

questions.q: Why did Tural's face go red?
options: The chicken was too hot and spicy
questions.why: “He tasted the meat and coughed loudly. His face went red. It was much too hot!”

questions.q: Nigar arrived and cooked the Mexican chicken again.
questions.why: False. They abandoned the chicken and “quickly cooked a nice homemade pasta.”

questions.q: The text says Tural thought it was “a piece of cake”. What does this idiom mean?
options: It needs a lot of sugar
questions.why: He thought making the dinner would be very simple after watching one video.

questions.q: What will Tural probably do for his next dinner party?
options: Cook a new foreign dish without help
Follow instructions carefully if he cooks
questions.why: “Next time, he decided, he will not cook without a recipe.”

B1.text:
Tural wanted to impress his new colleagues with a special dinner. He lived in a small flat near Nizami Street in Baku, and he usually just ordered pizza. However, this Friday, he decided to cook Asian cuisine. He watched a short video online and assumed the recipe was a piece of cake.

“It is just chicken and a few vegetables,” Tural confidently told his sister, Nigar, on the phone.

Tural went to the local market and bought all the necessary items. He loved spicy dishes, so he bought extra hot chillies. Back home, he chopped every ingredient and threw them into a massive pot. Unfortunately, he ended up making a huge portion for ten people, even though he had only invited three guests. Worse, he added a whole handful of chillies.

He tasted the sauce and immediately started coughing. His eyes watered. He quickly realised he had bitten off more than he could chew.

Half an hour later, Nigar knocked on the door. She walked in and stared at the disastrous kitchen.

“What on earth happened here?” she asked, smelling the strong smoke.

“I completely ruined the dinner,” Tural sighed. Nigar tasted the chicken and immediately grabbed a large glass of water.

“Okay, we definitely cannot serve this,” she said. “Let's go back to a local staple.”

They quickly cleaned the kitchen and prepared a traditional homemade plov with dried fruits and mild spices.

When the guests arrived, they sat down, displayed excellent table manners, and praised the beautiful meal.

“This rice is amazing,” his colleague Leyla smiled.

Tural looked at Nigar and laughed. He learned a valuable lesson: experimenting with food is fun, but sometimes the classics are safest.

questions.q: What is the main event of the story?
options: Tural teaches his sister how to make plov
Tural's colleagues complain about the food
Tural ruins an Asian dish and makes a local meal instead
Tural opens a restaurant in Baku
questions.why: He messes up the spicy Asian cuisine and his sister helps him make a traditional plov instead.

questions.q: Why did Tural make such a large amount of food?
options: He threw every ingredient in without planning
He invited ten people to the dinner
He wanted to have leftovers for a week
He bought a new giant pot on purpose
questions.why: “he chopped every ingredient and threw them into a massive pot. Unfortunately, he ended up making a huge portion for ten people”

questions.q: What did Nigar do right after she tasted the spicy sauce?
options: She threw the pot in the bin
She grabbed a large glass of water
questions.why: “Nigar tasted the chicken and immediately grabbed a large glass of water.”

questions.q: Tural usually cooks traditional Azerbaijani food on Fridays.
questions.why: False. The text says “he usually just ordered pizza.”

questions.q: Tural realised he had “bitten off more than he could chew”. What does this idiom mean?
options: He took a very big bite of chicken
He tried to do something that was too difficult for him
questions.why: He thought the complex meal would be easy, but it turned out to be too hard for him to manage.

questions.q: How did the guests feel about the dinner they actually ate?
options: They were very impressed and praised it
They thought it was too spicy
questions.why: They “praised the beautiful meal” and Leyla said “This rice is amazing”.

B2.text:
Tural had always believed that mastering a foreign cuisine was simply a matter of following instructions. Living in a modern apartment near Nizami Street, he usually relied on food delivery. However, when he invited his foreign colleagues over for Friday dinner, he decided to prepare a complex Thai delicacy. After skimming a five-minute tutorial, he was convinced the whole process would be a piece of cake.

“It’s basically just chicken, coconut milk, and some herbs,” Tural boasted to his sister, Nigar, over the phone. “I have it completely under control.”

He visited a specialty market in Baku to hunt down every exotic ingredient. Since he was a massive fan of spicy food, he doubled the amount of bird’s eye chillies the recipe recommended. Back in his kitchen, he started chopping and frying. Without measuring properly, he accidentally prepared a colossal portion meant to feed a dozen people, rather than a cosy group of four.

When the sauce began to bubble, Tural took a confident spoonful. Instantly, his throat tightened, his eyes streamed, and he broke into a sweat. As he gasped for air, it dawned on him that he had definitely bitten off more than he could chew.

Just then, Nigar let herself in with her spare key. She surveyed the smoke-filled kitchen and the mountain of burning pots.

“What is burning?” she asked, waving a towel to clear the air.

“My pride, mostly,” Tural croaked. “I can't possibly serve this. It is basically liquid fire.”

Nigar tried a tiny drop and immediately lunged for the milk. “Right, let’s abandon this disaster and whip up an Azerbaijani staple instead.”

Working together, they quickly assembled a rich, comforting homemade plov with chestnuts and dried apricots.

By the time the guests arrived, the flat smelled incredible. Throughout the evening, his colleagues demonstrated impeccable table manners and could not stop complimenting the authentic local dish.

“You know, trying to be someone you're not in the kitchen rarely works,” Nigar whispered to him as they cleared the plates.

Tural smiled, realising her words gave him some genuine food for thought. Next time, he would stick to the classics.

questions.q: What is the central theme of the story?
options: The difficulty of buying exotic ingredients in Baku
How to prepare a Thai delicacy step by step
The importance of table manners in business
A cooking failure that leads to appreciating familiar, traditional food
questions.why: Tural ruins a complex Thai dish but successfully pivots to a beloved local staple with his sister's help.

questions.q: Why did the Thai dish turn out so extremely spicy?
options: Tural purposely doubled the recommended amount of chillies
Tural used the wrong type of chilli
Nigar added extra spices by mistake
questions.why: “he doubled the amount of bird’s eye chillies the recipe recommended.”

questions.q: What was Nigar's first reaction when she entered the flat?
questions.why: “What is burning?” she asked, waving a towel to clear the air.

questions.q: Tural's colleagues realised that he did not cook the meal by himself.
questions.why: The text mentions they complimented the food, but does not state whether they knew Nigar helped cook it.

questions.q: What does “food for thought” mean in the context of the story?
options: An idea or lesson worth thinking about seriously
A physical meal that makes you full
questions.why: Nigar's advice about not pretending to be someone else gave him something serious to reflect on.

questions.q: What does Nigar imply when she says, “trying to be someone you're not in the kitchen rarely works”?
options: Tural should embrace his own culture rather than poorly copying others
Tural should have ordered delivery instead
Tural is a terrible cook and should give up
Tural needs to buy better kitchen equipment to cook Thai food
questions.why: She suggests he is better off cooking the traditional Azerbaijani staples he knows, rather than forcing an exotic cuisine.

podcast.title: What's on your plate?

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: What is one dish from your country every visitor must try? Guess: who in this episode cannot eat spicy food — Leyla or Sam?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. And I'm a little hungry, because today's topic is food and culture.
[laugh] Perfect timing. Sam, you came to my family's house last month. What did you eat?
Plov! Your mum's plov. Rice with saffron, meat, chestnuts, dried fruit... honestly, it was the best homemade meal of my year.
In Azerbaijani cuisine, plov is like a king. There are more than forty kinds.
Forty! And the portion she gave me was huge. Then she gave me a second one.
Of course. If your plate is empty, a mother thinks you're still hungry.
I learned that the hard way. [chuckle] I couldn't move for an hour.
So what's a staple food in England? Something people eat every day?
Bread and potatoes, I think. Simple food. But I love trying new things when I travel.
Even very spicy food?
[sigh] That's my weak point. In Thailand I ordered noodles that the waiter called 'a little hot'.
And?
I cried for ten minutes. Lesson learned: never bite off more than you can chew.
[laugh] Poor Sam. For me, the most interesting part of travel is trying a local delicacy, even a strange one.
Like what?
In Japan I tried raw sea urchin. The main ingredient is... well, the sea urchin. It tasted like the ocean.
Brave. Okay, let's talk about table manners. They're different everywhere, aren't they?
Very. Here we serve tea to guests again and again. In some countries you shouldn't finish everything; in others you should.
So the easy rule is: watch what your host does. It's a piece of cake.
Nice. And here's some food for thought: when you share a meal, you share a culture. Your question for your next SpeakLab call: what dish would you cook for a guest from abroad?
Not too spicy, please! See you next time.
[laugh] Bye for now!

questions.q: What is the episode mainly about?
options: Food, eating habits and manners in different cultures
questions.why: They talk about plov, spicy food, delicacies and table manners.

questions.q: Why couldn't Sam move for an hour after dinner?
options: Leyla's mum gave him two huge portions
questions.why: "The portion she gave me was huge. Then she gave me a second one."

questions.q: What happened to Sam in Thailand?
options: He ordered noodles that were far too spicy for him
questions.why: The waiter said 'a little hot' and Sam cried for ten minutes.

questions.q: Leyla did not like the sea urchin she tried in Japan.
questions.why: She says it tasted like the ocean, but not whether she liked it.

questions.q: Sam says: never "bite off more than you can chew". What does it mean?
options: Never try something too difficult for you
Never eat food you don't like
questions.why: The noodles were much too spicy for him — he took on more than he could handle.

questions.q: What is Sam's 'easy rule' for table manners in a new country?
questions.why: "The easy rule is: watch what your host does."

What is a table manner in your family that a visitor might not know?
